issues.quote: Four years on one watch, and he meant it to strike the first minute of the new century.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no duration for the repeater's making or any link between the watch and the new century.
issues.misreading: A solver could take 'four years' as a build-time hint and try to work out timing or a date from it. It has no bearing on the night's clock readings.

issues.quote: It has run badly for ten years.
issues.fact: The sheet only says 'my watch' for every reading. It does not say the watch is inaccurate or by how much.
issues.misreading: A solver could decide the watch's readings need correcting, or that its error is unknown, and so doubt the exact times Félix reports.

issues.quote: I thought he had dropped something, or that he was showing somebody the piece.
issues.fact: The sheet says only that a thump and the repeater were heard from the library. It places no one else in the atelier.
issues.misreading: 'Showing somebody the piece' suggests a visitor with the uncle at about 10:18, which the sheet does not give.

issues.quote: I had brandy, I will admit that, more than I should have.
issues.fact: The sheet does not mention drink or any effect on Félix's hearing or counting.
issues.misreading: A solver could doubt whether his counted notes or his watch readings were accurate because he had been drinking.
